rows.grounds: compound dharmin+rūpa; predicate describing ultimate reality
subject term identified in the statement
contrastive particle introducing the negated alternative
compound iti+arthaḥ; concluding gloss on the preceding discussion

items.question: Is ultimate reality constituted by the attribute-holder's nature or by the attribute's nature?
premises: Ultimate reality is identified as having the nature of the attribute-holder.
Ultimate reality is explicitly denied to have the nature of the attribute.
The statement presents the intended meaning of the preceding account.
items.inference: Therefore ultimate reality is the attribute-holder's nature alone, not the attribute's nature.
items.plain_english: The meaning is that the ultimate reality is of the nature of the attribute-holder alone, and not of the nature of the attribute.
